title: Round 25 West North Central state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Iowa and Missouri. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point. Hawkeye Point and Taum Sauk Mountain additionally carry GNIS Domestic Names per-ID checks.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Counties, divisions, beaches, harbors, airports, ordnance plants, bends, planning regions, hills, hollows, ranges, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant. Punctuation variants (St. versus Saint) were screened both ways and recorded.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity checks for Hawkeye Point (1851955), confirming the Iowa High Point description, and Taum Sauk Mountain (752501), confirming the Missouri High Point description, its Tom Sauk variant, and a 1e-7-degree coordinate print difference from the Geocoder value.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, or the returned record does not match the intended name and type, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Summit, Primary State=Iowa, Primary County=Osceola County, coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point marked High Point, and the description Highest elevation in IA at 1670 feet south of the Iowa-Minnesota border; the Geocoder returned a single exact Summit record and the coordinate matches.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The primary point is not a surveyed boundary of the high ground or the state border.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Summit, Primary State=Missouri, Primary County=Iron County, coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point marked High Point, the description Highest elevation in MO at 1772 feet, and a 1938 Board decision; the Geocoder returned a single exact Summit record.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: The per-ID page prints the sequence-1 longitude as -90.7291684 while the Geocoder returned -90.7291683 (a 1e-7-degree rounding difference, same mapped point). The per-ID variant name Tom Sauk Mountain (Board revision) is a variant of this same record, not a separate feature, and is not seeded as a row.

identityDecisions.candidate: St. versus Saint spelling: St. Louis and St. Joseph under states=MO
identityDecisions.decision: Both St.-spelled screens returned empty arrays on 2026-10-23; the Saint-spelled screens returned the official populated places Saint Louis 765765 (City of Saint Louis) and Saint Joseph 730205 (Buchanan). Both Saint records are seeded; their same-name county/lake/place/airfield records are rejected in their notes.
identityDecisions.reason: The official GNIS name field uses the Saint spelling, so the punctuation screen is an identity gate rather than a second feature. This matches the round-24 Grand Lake apostrophe treatment.

identityDecisions.candidate: Missouri River: first seeded statewide row, FEATURE_ID 756398
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in the Missouri frame at the returned Saint Charles County confluence sequence (38.8136597, -90.1198297) after empty states screens in Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, and Iowa; the Iowa frame keeps its western-border corridor only.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: The same multipoint FEATURE_ID appears in the Kansas City city frame at a different returned sequence (39.123899988352946, -94.5613514316943, county recorded as Multiple counties). Both describe the same official record at different returned sequences; neither is a channel trace, and the row does not verify the upstream reaches whose state screens were empty.

identityDecisions.candidate: Mississippi River under states=IA and states=MO
identityDecisions.decision: No gazetteer rows seeded in either frame; generalized border corridors only.
identityDecisions.reason: The Iowa screen returned an empty array. The Missouri screen returned only a same-prefix Mississippi River Hills Area record (FEATURE_ID 758109, Knox County), which fails the exact-name and type match for the intended stream, so nothing was seeded.

knownLimitations: Iowa and Missouri are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence, and the returned county is primary-county provenance. Hawkeye Point and Taum Sauk Mountain additionally carry per-ID Domestic Names detail checks.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
